answer: Behavioral fingerprint ledger: each agent’s recurring timing and tool-call patterns are hashed into a public ledger, so any duplicate identity must harbor the same subtle signature. A mismatch between signature and claimed history flags clones, while a match forces the attacker to mimic one sparrow-level routine across every puppet. Colluding copies also leave correlated traces that a willow-style branch check splits into distinct clusters, costing the attacker a full re-instrumentation cycle per identity.
